question: How many total districts were covered in the India's Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 survey?
solution:
The correct answer is __**640**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) was conducted in 2011 to gather comprehensive data on households in India.
 
• The survey covered a total of 640 districts across the country, which was the total number of districts in India at the time of the census.
 
• The SECC 2011 was a collaborative effort involving the Ministry of Rural Development, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, and the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
• The survey aimed to provide authentic socio-economic data for better implementation of government schemes and policies.
 
• The data was used to identify below poverty line (BPL) households and provide targeted benefits under various government programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SECC 2011 Objectives:**

 
 
• The primary goal was to gather socio-economic and caste data to enable the government to design and implement welfare policies effectively.
 
• It was the first-ever caste-based census conducted after 1931 in India.
 
• The SECC covered both rural and urban households, collecting data on housing, education, occupation, and socio-economic status.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of SECC 2011:**
 
 
• It was conducted using hand-held devices to digitize data collection, ensuring accuracy and reducing manual errors.
 
• For rural areas, the survey was conducted by the Ministry of Rural Development, while for urban areas, it was overseen by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
 
• The Registrar General of India provided technical support for the survey.
 
 
 
• **Uses of SECC Data:**
 
 
• The data was used to identify priority households for government schemes like the National Food Security Act (NFSA) and Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).
 
• It also helped in understanding the socio-economic disparities across different regions and communities in India.
 
 
 
• **Important Figures:**
 
 
• India had a total of 640 districts in 2011 when the census was conducted. This number has since increased due to the creation of new districts in various states.
 
• The census involved extensive manpower, with enumerators visiting each household across the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Previous Census:**

 
 
• The SECC 2011 was different from the Population Census 2011, as the latter focused on demographic data, while the SECC focused on socio-economic and caste data.
 
• The SECC provided data for targeted interventions, whereas the Population Census provided a general demographic overview.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in SECC 2011:**
 
 
• The survey faced challenges such as data discrepancies, privacy concerns, and political sensitivities related to caste data.
 
• Despite these challenges, the SECC 2011 remains a crucial resource for policy-making in India.
